The Eywa offline campaign toolkit is complete. Here's what I built and verified:

## Implementation (`/workspace/project`, 80 KB, 14 files)

| file | what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `campaign_cli.py` | strict JSON framing (64 MiB cap, duplicate keys, non-finite, invalid UTFâ8, trailing JSON â `{"error":"INVALID_INPUT"}`), always one JSON object, exit zero, boots local `src/` |
| `src/eywa/regex.py` | documented pattern grammar parser + Thompson NFA matcher over Latinâ1 (memoised transitions, nullable repetitions, escapes, classes/ranges) |
| `src/eywa/ast.py` | type lattice + acyclic forward-reference resolution, typed expression AST, JSON-expression compiler, evaluator (deep equality, exact `2^bits` modular arithmetic, lexical `all` shadowing, short-circuit connectives) |
| `src/eywa/oracles.py` | declaration postorder visitor; `LayoutBuilder` with the `MainBuilder` numbering convention (scalars, composites, string buffers, flag, widths); mirrored strict `ValueReader` recovery |
| `src/eywa/composer.py` | dependency graph with root-scoped lexicographic topological plan order; iterative transitive pipe composition and filter acceptance (no recursion limits on deep chains) |
| `src/eywa/wire.py` | strict KTEST v3 transport (base64, framing, canonical names, duplicates, trailing bytes, argument bounds) |
| `src/eywa/state.py` | guarded minimum-cost preparation: packed-key Dijkstra (cost, hops), tight-graph structure caching, lexicographic greedy walk |
| `src/eywa/run.py` | corpus identity (entry + recovered values, NUL-blind, result-blind) |
| `src/eywa/offline.py` | the pipeline integrating plans â recovery â attestation/filtering â reachability â corpus |

## Verification
- **Public fixtures**: 2/2 PASS via an equivalent bounded pipe runner (the supplied checker needs a `kill` overlay this sandbox denies).
- **25+ semantic fixtures** hand-computed: layout numbering across nested aliases/structs/arrays/strings, zero-length composites, void results, uint64, NUL constants vs recovery, transitive filter bindings, flag attestation, every `INVALID_TEST` class, precedence (transport â flag â filter â reachability â dedup), machine tie-breaks (cost â hops â lexicographic), guards, unreachable states.
- **Four fuzzers, zero failures**: state preparation vs brute-force enumeration (12k+ machines Ã all targets Ã all disabled sets), expressions vs an independently written evaluator (~3k typed cases), plan compilation vs an independent reference layout, and end-to-end value recovery with shuffled object order.
- **Scale**: 2.05 M objects/36 MB input 6.8 s; 4096 states Ã 16 k transitions Ã 2048 runs 2.4 s; 3.5 M preparation commands 2.2 s; 4.1 M match units 0.3 s; 3000-deep filter chain and 58-level type nesting fine â all far inside the 120 s budget.
